svg.title: Fabric IQ: The Ontology Layer Over OneLake Data
svg.desc: An architecture diagram: OneLake data (lakehouse tables, Eventhouse streams) is already modeled once by an existing Power BI semantic model. Fabric IQ's ontology item aligns itself from that semantic model rather than redefining business terms, then adds entity types, typed relationships, and a data-binding layer that maps physical columns to business concepts. That bound model is materialized into a queryable instance graph, built on the separate Graph in Microsoft Fabric item, which a tenant admin must enable before graph features work. NL2Ontology sits in front of the graph, translating natural-language business questions into structured queries constrained to the ontology's own published definitions. Two consumers sit downstream: a Fabric data agent answering ad hoc questions, and an operations agent polling the graph every 5 minutes for anomalies. A warning node covers the antipattern this layer exists to prevent — skipping the shared ontology and letting every AI system re-translate raw schema into business meaning by hand — and a second warning covers upstream data changes not auto-reflecting in the graph without an explicit refresh.
svg.text: Fabric IQ — the Ontology / Semantic Layer

g.title: Entity types, relationships, data binding — The ontology's structural core: reusable entity types, typed relationships, and a data-binding layer connecting them to OneLake.
g.text: Business concepts, relationships and rules modeled on top of existing data — no data movement — so AI agents reason from defined meaning, not raw schemas

svg.text: MICROSOFT IQ — ENTERPRISE INTELLIGENCE LAYER (FABRIC IQ IS ONE OF FOUR PILLARS)
TWO CORE FABRIC IQ ITEMS — DELIVERING UNIFIED DATA, BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE & OPERATIONAL INTELLIGENCE

g.title: Ontology generated/aligned from semantic model — The ontology bootstraps from the existing semantic model rather than being authored independently.
Existing semantic model — The production Power BI semantic model that already defines measures, relationships, and business-friendly names.
g.text: Curated analytics layer — measures, relationships, business-friendly fields

svg.text: Shared with the Power BI workload — items can belong to multiple workloads at once
Production BI investments bootstrap the ontology
Entities, relationships, properties, rules, and actions defined once

g.title: NL2Ontology — Converts a natural-language business question into a structured query, constrained to the ontology's own published definitions.
g.text: Exposes NL2Ontology — converts business questions into structured queries

svg.text: Enables cross-domain reasoning via graph traversal

g.title: Antipattern: skipping the shared ontology — Without a shared ontology, every AI system must manually re-translate raw schema into business meaning — inconsistently.
g.text: AI systems are described as unfit for high-stakes decisions — every business question otherwise requires manual translation by a domain expert from raw tables/schemas into business concepts.

g.title: Queryable instance graph — Entity instances as nodes, asserted/derived links as edges — the materialized, traversable form of the ontology.
g.text: IQ (PREVIEW) WORKLOAD — ITEMS GROUPED AROUND THE ONTOLOGY (MOST SHARED WITH OTHER WORKLOADS)

g.title: Operations agent (continuous, polling) — Continuously monitors the graph for anomalies and can propose or trigger governed actions, on a 5-minute cadence.

svg.text: AI EXPERIENCES — NAVIGATE DEFINED MEANING, NOT RAW SCHEMAS

g.title: Fabric data agent (reactive) — Answers ad hoc natural-language questions, grounded in the ontology rather than raw schema.

svg.text: Virtual analyst for a domain, grounded in semantic models and ontologies — publishable to Microsoft 365, Foundry, Copilot Studio, and custom apps
Benefits: faster onboarding (concepts declared once) and governance (consistent definitions enforced across teams)

g.title: Antipattern: assuming real-time graph freshness — Upstream data changes are not automatically reflected in the ontology's graph without an explicit refresh.
g.text: Not formally listed as an IQ workload item, but every IQ item relies on and interacts natively with OneLake data tables

svg.text: Reached across clouds and on-premises via shortcuts, mirroring, and the OneLake catalog — the same governed data grounds models, ontologies, and agents

g.title: OneLake data (lakehouse, Eventhouse) — The underlying business data — lakehouse tables and Eventhouse streams — that everything in Fabric IQ ultimately traces back to.
g.text: No data duplication: the ontology models meaning on top of tables that already live in OneLake

svg.text: grounded in existing OneLake tables — no data movement

g.title: Graph in Microsoft Fabric (tenant setting) — The separate Graph item and its tenant-level enablement toggle — a prerequisite most teams don't expect.
g.text: Fabric Codex — original diagram, July 2026. Not a Microsoft asset; conceptual (L1–L2), grounded in fabric-iq-overview.json.
